report:
## Conclusion

**Yes — corticosteroids such as dexamethasone have been shown to improve survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients, and this is now standard-of-care worldwide.** However, the benefit is limited to patients with severe or critical disease (those requiring supplemental oxygen or mechanical ventilation); there is no evidence of benefit, and possible harm, in patients with mild disease who do not need respiratory support.

### Key Evidence

1. **The RECOVERY Trial** (University of Oxford, published in *NEJM*, July 2020) randomly assigned over 6,000 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to receive 6 mg of dexamethasone daily for up to 10 days or usual care. Dexamethasone **reduced deaths by one-third** in patients on mechanical ventilation (rate ratio 0.65, p=0.0003) and **by one-fifth** in patients receiving oxygen only. No mortality benefit was observed in patients not receiving respiratory support.
   - Source: https://www.recoverytrial.net/news/low-cost-dexamethasone-reduces-death-by-up-to-one-third-in-hospitalised-patients-with-severe-respiratory-complications-of-covid-19
   - Source: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436

2. **The WHO REACT Meta-Analysis** (published in *JAMA*, September 2020) pooled data from seven randomized trials of critically ill COVID-19 patients treated with systemic corticosteroids (dexamethasone, hydrocortisone, or methylprednisolone) versus usual care or placebo. It found that corticosteroid administration was **associated with significantly lower 28-day all-cause mortality**.
   - Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32876694/

3. **WHO Guidance** (updated 2025) explicitly recommends corticosteroids — especially dexamethasone — as **lifesaving medicines for patients with severe or critical COVID-19**, to be given alongside other standard therapies.
   - Source: https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-dexamethasone

### Bottom Line
Dexamethasone and similar corticosteroids reduce mortality in the most severely ill COVID-19 patients (those on oxygen or ventilators). They do not help — and may harm — patients with mild disease. This evidence is robust, replicated across multiple trials, and endorsed by major health authorities including WHO and IDSA.
